evidence: alert-triage/main.py:550-556 sets `confidence = 0.75` then only overwrites it if `re.search(r'```json\s*\{[^}]*"confidence"\s*:\s*([0-9.]+)[^}]*\}\s*```', answer)` matches. A regex MISS keeps the 0.75 default with NO logging. The SYSTEM_PROMPT (line 505-507) demands the fence appear LAST, after all four ## sections, and says 'If data is empty ... set confidence < 0.3' — but that instruction only takes effect if the model both emits the exact fence AND the fence survives. On truncation the fence is dropped: llm_client.py:284/312-316 shows `llm_complete` returns the truncated `result` as-is (only logs a `finish_reason in (max_tokens,length)` warning) — the trailing fence is exactly what gets cut, so the miss falls back to HIGH. Same defect, same regex, higher-risk defaults: ql-2 athena-hunter/main.py:651-657 `confidence = 0.7`; ql-3 thousandeyes-analyst/main.py:504-510 `confidence = 0.7`. So a max_tokens truncation or a model that scores confidence in prose reports fabricated 0.7-0.75 confidence, directly inverting each prompt's own 'confidence < 0.3 when empty' rule. Miss is plausible: flash-lite with thinking_budget clamped 0->-1 (llm_client.py:178-180) emits variable-length output; TE max_tokens=2000 (below the others' 4096) with 30 tests routinely truncates (see lo-3). Real operator-trust problem: the fallback is HIGH, not neutral, and silent.
fix: Change the fallback to a low/neutral sentinel that signals 'unparseable', not high confidence. Minimal: set the pre-regex default to e.g. `confidence = 0.3` in all three files (alert-triage:550, athena-hunter:651, thousandeyes:504), and/or log a warning on regex miss. Better: derive a max-confidence cap from `get_last_llm_metrics()['finish_reason']` — if it is max_tokens/length, force confidence <= 0.3. Single shared helper in agents/shared would DRY all three.

evidence: thousandeyes-analyst/main.py:141-163 `fetch_all_tests` wraps the entire body in `try/except Exception` and returns `[]` on ANY failure (auth 401/expiry, 5xx, wrong account group 403, network) — indistinguishable from a genuinely empty inventory. gather_te_context:348-354 then branches `if not tests:` and returns `{total_tests:0, active_alert_count, active_alerts, note:'no tests configured'}` with NO `error` field and NO `monitoring_available:False`. Contrast the blank-token branch at 332-338 which DOES set `monitoring_available:False` + `error`, and the per-test unknown state at 303-311 (sweep-3 fixes). The inventory-fetch-failure branch was NOT covered. Downstream: llm_analyze prompt (line 459-461) says 'confidence < 0.3 only when ... error field set in context' — but this branch has no error field, so the model reports normal confidence (~0.6-0.7) and 'no tests configured' reads to an operator as 'monitoring fine, nothing to test.' A dead feed thus reads as all-clear. Confirmed blind-vs-empty conflation at the inventory level.
fix: Distinguish fetch failure from empty inventory. Minimal: have `fetch_all_tests` signal failure rather than returning bare `[]` — e.g. raise, or return a sentinel; then in gather_te_context, on failure return `{error:'test inventory fetch failed', monitoring_available:False, total_tests:0}` mirroring the blank-token branch. Simplest concrete change: catch the fetch exception inside gather_te_context (call fetch_all_tests without its internal swallow, or add a companion `fetch_all_tests_or_raise`) and set the error/monitoring_available flags so the < 0.3 confidence + 'monitoring blind' path triggers.

evidence: There IS a real fixable code defect independent of LLM variance. The NL answer and the structured severity_breakdown are derived from DIFFERENT data. severity_breakdown (alert-triage/main.py:732,767,774-784) is computed by `_severity_breakdown`, which normalizes every alert via `_norm_sev` (line 779) into word buckets {critical,high,medium,low,informational}. But the answer is produced by the LLM from `prioritized_alerts` (line 731 = `enriched_alerts[:15]`), which are the RAW alert dicts: correlate_alerts_with_flows:394 does `{**alert, ...}` and never normalizes, so Suricata/Corelight rows still carry `alert_severity`/`severity` = the VARCHAR numbers '1'/'2'/'3' (see NUM_SEV comment lines 80-83). So the LLM literally sees `"severity": "2"` and free-texts 'severity 2 informational' (its own guess at what '2' means) while the normalized breakdown correctly says medium:95/low:55. This is exactly the ql-8 numeric-vs-word mapping issue surfacing in prose. The two can and do disagree because one side is normalized and the other is not. The run-to-run flip ('severity 2 informational' vs '95 medium') is LLM nondeterminism ON TOP of the defect, but feeding unnormalized severity is the fixable root cause.
fix: Normalize severity in the alerts before they go into triage_data['prioritized_alerts']. Minimal: in correlate_alerts_with_flows (or just before building triage_data), overwrite each alert's severity with `_norm_sev(...)` so the LLM sees the same word buckets the breakdown uses — e.g. add `"severity": _norm_sev(alert.get('severity', alert.get('alert_severity','low')))` into the enriched dict. Then the prose and the structured breakdown draw from one normalized source and cannot report mismatched labels.

evidence: (a) CONFIRMED: the answer is returned raw with no scratchpad stripping. llm_client._extract_content:208-221 only joins text blocks and `.strip()`s whitespace; thousandeyes llm_analyze:489-512 returns `answer` verbatim. thinking_budget=0 is clamped to -1 (dynamic thinking) for flash-lite (llm_client.py:178-180), so the model CAN emit reasoning; nothing removes any pre-'## Answer' preamble, so scratchpad like '...let's list the distinct ones...## Answer' passes straight through to the client. (b) CONFIRMED relatively: TE uses max_tokens=2000 (main.py:493) vs 4096 in alert-triage (line 531) and athena-hunter (line 638) — TE has the lowest budget, and 30 tests + leaked reasoning easily blows past it, triggering the max_tokens truncation that also drops the trailing confidence fence (feeding ql-3). (c) PARTIAL: the aggregate roll-up DOES carry the unknown state correctly — gather_te_context:379-392 computes unknown_count and returns it, and summary_data:577 exposes unknown_count=30 in the JSON response. So the structured data is right; the '0 healthy, 0 degraded, 0 failing' with unknown omitted is the LLM free-texting green/yellow/red counts and dropping the '+ U could not be measured' clause the prompt demands (lines 438-439) — worsened by truncation cutting that clause. That part is LLM-noncompliance/token-budget, not a data-layer bug.
fix: (a) Strip everything before the first '## Answer' in the returned answer (in llm_analyze, before confidence extraction: `answer = answer[answer.find('## Answer'):] if '## Answer' in answer else answer`). (b) Raise TE max_tokens to 4096 to match the other agents. (c) Since unknown_count is already in the structured data, prepend a deterministic verdict line to the answer built from the rollup counts (e.g. f'{green} healthy, {yellow+red} degraded, {unknown} could not be measured') instead of trusting the model to emit it — closes both the display gap and the LLM-omission.
